summary: John Stratton Hawley is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Amherst College and under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held posts at Bowdoin College and Columbia University, where he became a professor around 1986.
John Stuart Mill was a philosopher who studied at University College London from around 1828 to 1830. He held a post at the East India Company from approximately 1823 to 1858.

John Sydenham Furnivall was a historian who studied at Trinity Hall, Trinity College, and the wider University of Cambridge, as well as Leiden University. He founded the Burma Research Society in 1910 and held a post at Cambridge (~1936–1941).

John Taber is an Indology and philosophy scholar who earned his D.Phil. at the University of Hamburg, studying under Lambert Schmithausen and Reiner Wiehl. He taught at Case Western Reserve University (~1982–1989) and the University of New Mexico (~1989–2021).

John Thompson Platts was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Bedford School and Balliol College, Oxford. He served at Saugor High School, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and became Teacher of Persian at the University of Oxford in 1880.

John Vincent Bellezza is a scholar of Tibetology and archaeology who studied under Yungdrung Tenzin and Tshering Choephel. He was affiliated with the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences as attested in 2014.

John W. Pettit is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed undergraduate studies at Haverford College, did doctoral work under Robert A. F. Thurman, and studied under Dilgo Khyentse, Ashok Gangadean, Lal Mani Joshi, Gunapala Dharmasiri, and Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa.

John W. Schroeder is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. After studying at Los Angeles Valley College and the University of Oregon (under Don S. Levi and Hee-Jin Kim), he held posts at Oregon, College of Wooster, and St. Mary's College of Maryland.
John W. Spellman was an Indologist and historian. He held academic posts at the University of Washington (~1964–1967) and served as a professor at the University of Windsor (~1967–1999).

John Wilson was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Edinburgh (1819–1828). He founded Wilson College, served as President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1835–1842), and was Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1869).

John Woodroffe was an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at University College, Oxford (~1884–1888). He served as a judge at the Calcutta High Court, Tagore Law Professor at the University of Calcutta, and Reader in Indian Law at Oxford.
Join Saeki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sennyu-ji and under Sadatomo Chihaya. He held posts at Hōryū-ji, Hōryūji Kangakuin, the Imperial Academy, and the University of Tokyo.

Joji Fujii is a scholar of Japanese history who completed his studies at Kyoto University between approximately 1966 and 1974. He later held an academic post at Kyoto University from around 1989 to 2011.

Jokai Hiraoka was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1944–1948) and Kyoto University (~1948–1953). He served as a professor at Otemae University (~1966–1989) and taught at Shuchiin University (~1989–1999).

Jon Kabat-Zinn works in religious studies and medicine, having studied at Haverford College and MIT, alongside meditation training under Philip Kapleau, Thich Nhat Hanh, and Seungsahn Haengwon. He founded UMass Memorial Medical Center and held posts at UMass Chan Medical School.

Jonardon Ganeri is a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Cambridge and Oxford (D.Phil. under Bimal Krishna Matilal). He has held professorships at Nottingham, Liverpool, Sussex, Monash, New York University, and the University of Toronto.

Jonathan A. Silk is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied at Oberlin, Michigan (under Luis O. Gómez), and Ryukoku. He held posts at Grinnell, Western Michigan, Yale, UCLA, and Leiden University.

Jonathan C. Gold is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He has held teaching posts at the University of Vermont, Drew University (attested 2006), and Princeton University (attested 2015–2016).

Jonathan Christopher Cleary was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who completed his doctoral work at Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi (~1976–1984). He held an instructor post at Wesleyan University from around 1984 to 1986.

Jonathan Geen is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies who earned his doctorate at McMaster University under Phyllis Granoff. He has held teaching posts at McMaster University, Butler University, and the University of Rochester.
